newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones sees 96 earnings below $1.96/shr.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones sees 96 earnings below $1.96/shr.

text.p: Dow Jones & Co Inc said on Tuesday its 1996 earnings would be slightly lower than the $1.96 per share earned in 1995, because of increased expenses.

"As expense increases continue to outpace revenue gains in this segment of our business, we believe Dow Jones' 1996 earnings will be slightly lower than the $1.96 a share earned in 1995," said Peter Kann, chairman and chief executive officer.
The First Call mean earnings estimate for the year was $2.03 per share.

Dow Jones announced third quarter earnings of $0.42 per share versus $0.35 per share in the same quarter last year, including a $0.09 per share gain from the sale of its minority interest in Press-Enterprises Co.

The company, which publishes The Wall Street Journal and Barron's magazine as well as electronic information, said an operating decline in the financial information services segment hurt its quarterly results.

"Although very strong operating income gains were posted by our businesss publishing and community newspapers segments, earnings were adversely affected by an operating income decline in the financial information services segment," Kann said.

Operating income at Ottaway Newspapers, Dow's community newspaper subsidiary, rose 57.6 percent to $11.4 million, the company said. The business publishing segment had third quarter operating income of $24.3 million, nearly five times last year's income, it said.
